product: Military vehicles (Boxer, Lynx, Puma, Wolf Pack), weapons and ammunition (155mm artillery, tank ammunition, propellant), air defence (Skynex, Skyranger), digital systems (TaWAN, D-LBO, drones, simulation) and naval ships; also civilian e-mobility and capacitors.
demand: Strong and policy driven: NATO 5% of GDP target, rising German and eastern-European defence budgets, Ukraine rearmament. H1 2026 backlog EUR 80.5bn and Nomination EUR 16.2bn, with Q2 operating margin at a 17.1% high.
pricing_power: Mixed but improving: group operating margin 15.0% in H1 and 23.7% in Weapon and Ammunition, driven by mix and leverage. Real pricing power on scarce ammunition and propellant capacity, but capped by monopsony government customers and fixed framework terms.
competition: European and global primes: KNDS, BAE Systems, Leonardo, Thales, Hensoldt, Saab, Kongsberg, plus TKMS in naval and Hyundai Rotem and US artillery makers. Rheinmetall positions itself as a land, sea, air and space full-spectrum player versus these peers.
team: CEO and board chairman Armin Papperger, in post since 2013 and president of the German defence industry association. CFO Klaus Neumann; board members include Dr. Vera Saal and Rene Gansauge. Papperger fronts the Q2 conference call on 2026-08-06.
market_strategy: Expand capacity (Aschau powder plant, new Lithuanian plant, UK pipe output), broaden from land into sea, air and space, lock in multi-year framework agreements, and grow the international share, which reached 62% of H1 2026 sales.
bull: H1 2026 sales +39% to EUR 5.227bn, operating result +74% to EUR 786m, margin 15.0%, Q2 margin 17.1%, backlog EUR 80.5bn, 62% international; Bernstein PT 1900 and RBC Outperform 1600 dated Sep 2026.
bear: 2026-06-24 F126 frigate cancellation cut guidance EUR 300m; H1 operating free cash flow -EUR 1.616bn; JPMorgan negative catalyst watch 2026-09-10; MWB Sell-to-Neutral 2026-09-02; share -47% y/y; backlog includes uncommitted call-offs.
falsifier: Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-05 show 2026 sales guidance below EUR 13.7bn or group operating margin below 15%, or operating free cash flow still negative.
web_what_changed: 2026-08-06 H1 results: sales +39% to EUR 5.227bn, operating result +74% to EUR 786m, margin 15.0%, EPS 8.43. Guidance cut by EUR 300m to EUR 13.7-14.2bn after Germany cancelled the F126 frigate on 2026-06-24. Backlog EUR 80.5bn. Artillery order 2026-09-14; customs-vessel maintenance 2026-09-23.
web_not_known_yesterday: Little genuinely new on 2026-09-24/25. The share closed at EUR 989.10 on Xetra (delayed) on 2026-09-25, below EUR 1,000. MWB Research reiterated its neutral rating after the share fell under EUR 1,000 (2026-09-24).
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and mix. Management credits the production ramp-up plus a favourable product mix and operating leverage, with Q2 margin 17.1%. No explicit price contribution is disclosed; demand is government-budget driven rather than price driven.
web_suppliers: In-house propellant through Nitrochemie Aschau (powder plant about EUR 350m, 4,200 t per year, production 2027, full 2028). Mercedes-Benz supplies the W464 base platform; blackned GmbH is a digital partner. Constrained: Europe-wide gunpowder and nitrocellulose bottleneck, framed as Project Firepower; new capacity is years away.
web_customers: Governments. Germany was 38% of H1 sales and Europe 42.9%. Main customers: Bundeswehr (Puma, Lynx, vehicles), Ukraine (artillery), Hungary, Poland, Romania under SAFE, UK, US Marine Corps, plus naval buyers. Highly concentrated in a few state budgets.
web_who_loses: TKMS won the F126 frigate order that Rheinmetall unit NVL lost; rival primes KNDS, BAE Systems, Leonardo, Thales, Hensoldt, Saab and Kongsberg lose share in vehicles, ammunition and air defence; artillery importers lose as Rheinmetall in-house powder capacity grows.
web_contradicting_evidence: The 2026-06-24 F126 cancellation exposed political programme risk and cut 2026 guidance by EUR 300m; H1 operating free cash flow was negative EUR 1.616bn. mwb Research rates Sell and JPMorgan set a Negative Catalyst Watch on 2026-09-10; the share is down about 47% year on year despite record orders; backlog includes uncommitted framework call-offs.
web_if_management_right: 2026 sales reach EUR 13.7-14.2bn at about 19% margin; the EUR 80.5bn backlog converts into revenue as capacity ramps up (powder 2027-28, Lithuania); margins and cash flow improve; the share re-rates toward the consensus target of EUR 1,641 (median about EUR 1,500).
web_if_management_wrong: Execution or funding slippage: inventory build and negative cash flow worsen; further cancellations or a Ukraine ceasefire cut demand; the 19% margin guidance is missed; naval losses persist; the EUR 80.5bn backlog fails to convert, so earnings and the valuation multiple compress together.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Suppliers and partners: Mercedes-Benz (W464 platform), blackned GmbH, steel and electronics vendors, nitrocellulose and cotton-linter chemical suppliers, shipyards NVL and Blohm+Voss, Provectus Robotics, plus European logistics, testing and sub-tier defence subcontractors.
